snapshot.supervisor_frontier: 9.13AY P0_RESOURCE_GUARD: missing container cgroup telemetry is UNKNOWN, not healthy

source_findings.finding: cgroup v2 provides workload-scope accounting surfaces including cpu.stat, memory.current/memory.peak/memory.stat and pids.current; memory.peak is scoped to a cgroup and descendants.
source_findings.architecture_implication: When an exact container cgroup identity is available, cgroup-v2 is the preferred resource-accounting witness tier.

source_findings.finding: Podman --cgroups=disabled explicitly forces a container not to create cgroups.
source_findings.architecture_implication: A no-cgroup container is a legitimate runtime state; absence must not be silently repaired by relabeling host metrics as container metrics.

source_findings.finding: Podman stats relies on cgroup information for resource statistics.
source_findings.architecture_implication: Native Podman resource statistics are not an independent replacement for missing cgroup accounting.

source_findings.finding: Podman top can expose host PIDs for container processes when its process-discovery path works.
source_findings.architecture_implication: Process identity may be useful as a degraded observation input but does not itself establish container resource-accounting completeness.

source_findings.finding: Podman records the container process PID in a pidfile and documents discovery of that pidfile through inspect.
source_findings.architecture_implication: The exact container init host PID can seed a process-scoped degraded witness if bound to process-incarnation evidence.

source_findings.finding: /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children only reports first-level children and explicitly does not guarantee precise live results; children can be skipped unless inspected processes are stopped/frozen for precision.
source_findings.architecture_implication: Recursive procfs children enumeration must never be promoted to exact live container membership. It is DEGRADED/PARTIAL unless a stronger independent membership witness exists.

source_findings.finding: /proc/PID/smaps_rollup supplies per-process pre-summed memory-map metrics and the kernel documents races in proc memory-map reads.
source_findings.architecture_implication: smaps_rollup can support bounded process-level memory evidence, not exact whole-container accounting. PSS is preferable to naively summing RSS when shared mappings matter, but process-set completeness remains a separate requirement.

source_findings.finding: pidfd_open is the preferred stable reference for an already-existing process and avoids relying solely on a recyclable numeric PID.
source_findings.architecture_implication: A process-scoped fallback should bind numeric PID to process-incarnation evidence, ideally pidfd while live and/or /proc starttime in persisted evidence.

f2_source_observations.finding: WP1201 already encodes explicit OBSERVED versus UNKNOWN host facts and forbids invented defaults; it is host fingerprint evidence, not resource telemetry or completion evidence.

WP605 accepts caller-supplied whole-child cpu_time_ns and peak_rss_bytes bound to exact child reconciliation/provenance, but the source does not define how missing cgroup coverage becomes exact container-scope measurement.

Existing AgentCgroup research already forbids parent endpoint RSS => child/tool peak promotion and requires UNKNOWN/DEGRADED observer coverage. This objective therefore does not reopen that E5 candidate.

requirements: exact cgroup identity/path bound to container/runtime identity
best_supported_witness_ladder.credit: container-scope resource measurement evidence only; no isolation-health/completion credit by itself

requirements: exact container init PID or runtime process identity
process-incarnation binding via pidfd and/or starttime
best_supported_witness_ladder.credit: partial process-scoped evidence only; no claim of complete container accounting when membership is not exact

negative_results: Host free memory/disk/uptime cannot substitute for container-scope accounting.
A clean exact-source worktree solves source provenance but does not solve resource-observer scope.
Podman stats is not independent of cgroup accounting.
Recursive /proc children traversal is not exact live container membership.
Numeric PID alone is insufficient durable process-incarnation identity.
Summed process RSS is not an exact whole-container memory metric and can mis-account shared pages.
hypothesis: F2 should represent resource evidence as an explicit witness tier/scope rather than one undifferentiated healthy/unhealthy field, preserving UNKNOWN whenever neither exact cgroup accounting nor a bounded process-scoped witness is available.
counterhypothesis: Current WP1201 host profile plus WP605 caller-supplied telemetry may already be sufficient if target-runtime acceptance simply refuses resource promotion when cgroup is unavailable; a new typed resource-witness structure may be unnecessary complexity.
next_discriminator: Map the current target-runtime/host-profile/WP605 integration surfaces and determine whether the witness ladder can be expressed using existing provenance/UNKNOWN fields without adding a new canonical schema. Prefer no new structure if existing typed evidence can preserve scope exactly.
